name: MS Quarantine for Splunk SOAR
description: Ingest Microsoft Defender quarantine emails through Azure Automation into native SOAR or ES workflows. Inspect, release, deny and reconcile quarantine messages.

actions.description: Read-only inspection of the deployed runbook, loaded Exchange cmdlet contract, and one exact quarantine identity; optional tenant RBAC inspection requires explicit opt-in
actions.verbose: Fires the Azure Automation webhook with action=diagnose. The runbook binds the exact Get-QuarantineMessage identity before any optional tenant-wide RBAC query. By default it reads only the identity and local runtime/cmdlet metadata. When include_rbac=true, it additionally reads management-role contracts, the Quarantine role and assignments, managed-identity app/object GUIDs, the matching Exchange service principal, and relevant role-group membership. Only GUID-confirmed matching group names cross into the result; unrelated assignment names and members remain private. Permission-query totals count every real failure while retained records are capped at 20 and 32 KiB of compact UTF-8 JSON. It never returns an access token or xms_mirid resource path and never invokes Release-QuarantineMessage.

identity.description: Exact quarantine Identity in GUID1\GUID2 form. The diagnose action reads this identity but never releases or denies it.

include_rbac.description: Explicitly opt in to tenant-wide read-only RBAC and role-group diagnostics after the exact quarantine identity has been bound. Defaults to false.

actions.description: Release a quarantined message to all original recipients
actions.verbose: Fires the Azure Automation webhook with action=release. The runbook confirms the exact Identity matches the asset-selected source status (Requested by default, NotReleased for needs_review) and then invokes Release-QuarantineMessage -Identity <id> -ReleaseToAll -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction Stop exactly once, with no synthetic binder or capability gate and no automatic retry. Native cmdlet/binder errors, the exact-identity postcondition and the effective Exchange sign-in (always the Automation Account Managed Identity, plus organization and its source; never secrets) are reported separately; cleanup never overrides them. Before every write a read-only config_check proves that the protocol minimum Runbook 3.4.2+ applies the Managed Identity-only connection and the configured organization. It then performs a bounded postcondition window (default seven exact reads at ten-second intervals). Only Released is success. A deterministic rejection with an unchanged source state is confirmed_failed; ambiguous outcomes remain outcome_unknown and block blind retry. Successful diagnostics are compact unless enabled on the asset. IRREVERSIBLE. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/release-quarantinemessage Needs review uses the quarantine_selection_v1 pairing check and requires protocol minimum Runbook 3.4.3 or newer. The recommended pair is App 3.7.4 / Runbook 3.4.5 for bounded/redacted disposition diagnostics. Deny of a message without a release request is tenant-unverified; only confirmed Denied is success.

identity.description: Quarantine message Identity in the exact format GUID1\GUID2 (e.g. c14401cf-aa9a-465b-cfd5-08d0f0ca37c5\4c2ca98e-94ea-db3a-7eb8-3b63657d4db7). Use container:data.quarantine_identity from the ingested SOAR event or quarantine_identity from the ES finding. The format is validated before the webhook fires - malformed values fail immediately without starting a runbook job.

operation_id.description: Stable idempotency key for this logical release. Reusing the same value suppresses another webhook while its operation record is retained. Terminal records may be evicted at the 50-record registry limit; this is not permanent idempotency protection. If omitted, the connector derives a stable key from the SOAR container, action, and identity.

example_values: Release request approval confirmed by Exchange quarantine status.

The runbook confirms the exact Identity matches the asset-selected source status (Requested by default, NotReleased for needs_review) and then invokes Release-QuarantineMessage -Identities @(<id>) -ActionType Deny -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction Stop exactly once, with no synthetic binder or capability gate and no automatic retry. Native cmdlet/binder errors, the exact-identity postcondition and the effective Exchange sign-in (always the Automation Account Managed Identity, plus organization and its source; never secrets) are reported separately; cleanup never overrides them. Before every write a read-only config_check proves that the protocol minimum Runbook 3.4.2+ applies the Managed Identity-only connection and the configured organization. It then performs a bounded postcondition window (default seven exact reads at ten-second intervals). Only Denied is success. A deterministic rejection with an unchanged source state is confirmed_failed; ambiguous outcomes remain outcome_unknown and block blind retry. Successful diagnostics are compact unless enabled on the asset. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/release-quarantinemessage#-actiontype Needs review uses the quarantine_selection_v1 pairing check and requires protocol minimum Runbook 3.4.3 or newer. The recommended pair is App 3.7.4 / Runbook 3.4.5 for bounded/redacted disposition diagnostics. Deny of a message without a release request is tenant-unverified; only confirmed Denied is success.

actions.description: Read an existing Azure job and optionally refresh the exact Exchange status without a disposition call
actions.verbose: READ-ONLY. By default, queries only the supplied Azure Automation job/output and never invokes the webhook. If refresh_exchange_status is explicitly enabled for a completed outcome_unknown job, it starts the paired runbook's action=reconcile path, which performs exactly one Get-QuarantineMessage read and cannot invoke Release-QuarantineMessage. The durable operation is updated only after action, identity, version, and postcondition evidence validate.

azure_job_id.description: Existing Azure Automation job UUID recorded by the original release or deny action.

expected_action.description: Irreversible action the existing job was expected to execute.

expected_identity.description: Exact quarantine identity expected in the validated runbook result.

operation_id.description: Optional stable operation ID from the original action. When omitted, the connector resolves it from the Azure job ID or creates a durable read-only observation.

refresh_exchange_status.description: Explicitly start one read-only runbook reconciliation to obtain a fresh exact Exchange ReleaseStatus. No release or deny cmdlet is permitted.
